editorial.headline: Money Market Funds: Nationally Open, Closed to PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Money market fund activity can be wholly foreign-owned nationally, yet Bali’s PMA moratorium prevents a foreign investor from registering it at a Bali address.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register money market fund activity as PMA at a Bali address today. That conclusion sits beside—not against—the national position: KBLI 64310 is TERBUKA nationally, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. The divergence is the essential fact for a founder considering this classification. National openness establishes the permitted ownership ceiling; Bali’s rule determines whether PMA registration is available at all in the province. Each part of the record must be read in its own jurisdictional setting.

KBLI 64310 covers money market fund activity. Its core is a collective investment scheme that gathers money from the public by issuing shares or units, then invests the proceeds primarily in short-term assets. The record identifies assets with a maturity of one year or less as the example of this short duration. The units can be regarded as substitutes similar to deposits. These details give the activity its shape: public capital is pooled, participation is represented through shares or units, and the investment focus is primarily short term. The classification is framed around that collective scheme and the uses to which its proceeds are put.

As to scale, the activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. Those are the four business-scale labels expressly listed, from Mikro through Besar. In the national PMA setting, the TERBUKA designation is paired with maximum foreign ownership of 100%. In direct terms, a foreign stake may reach 100% nationally. The scale listing and the foreign-ownership ceiling are complementary facts: the first sets out the listed scales open to the activity, while the second conveys the national limit on foreign participation.

Bali’s position is materially stricter. The record marks it CHIUSO_MORATORIA_BALI and confirms that PMA registration is blocked. The stated reason is that, at the Besar scale, the activity is classified as Rendah, bringing it within Bali’s PMA moratorium. The provincial rule blocks PMA for activities in the low- and medium-low-risk bands throughout Bali, on a permanent basis. The result is categorical for a Bali address: no PMA registration route is available today, notwithstanding the national 100% ceiling. This is not a Bali-specific reduction in the foreign stake; it is a block on PMA registration in Bali.
